message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More | |-------|------------|--------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Guidelines | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for drivers over 18, but all passengers must buckle. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI Enforcement | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Yield” signs require slowing and giving way to traffic already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Do not exceed the speed limit when overtaking. | TxDOT – Safe Driving Practices | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in a driveway or on a private property without permission.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (except some exempt categories). | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) – Vehicle Registration | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or obstructing traffic.
• The towing company must notify the owner and the police. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens.
• Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Roadside Assistance & Breakdown** | • If your vehicle breaks down, move it to the shoulder and activate hazard lights.
• Call 911 if you’re in danger. | TxDOT – Roadside Assistance | | **Special Situations** | • **Winter Weather**: Use chains or winter tires if required by law.
• **Construction Zones**: Follow posted signs and reduced speed limits. | TxDOT – Weather‑Related Driving | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **TxDOT Safety Resources** – Tips, videos, and updates on road safety. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/safety 3. **TxDMV** – Information on registration, inspections, and driver licensing. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances or recent changes. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a simple but effective safety measure. - **Avoid distractions** – especially cell‑phone use; use hands‑free if you must talk. - **Observe posted speed limits** – they’re designed for safety and can vary widely. - **Be mindful of school buses and pedestrians** – they have priority. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help prevent accidents. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, recent changes, or how to handle a particular driving scenario!
